TITLE:    [**Hospital Unit Name 6469**] NOTE
   Chief Complaint:  Hemoptysis
   HPI:
   46yo M w/ h/o alpha-1 anti-trypsin deficiency, and asthma, w/ recent
   gastric band placed in [**Month (only) **]. who now p/w hemptysis x7-10d. He was in his
   USOH, w/ his baseline DOE from walking the distance of east to [**Hospital Ward Name **] or 1 flight of stairs, good appetitie, and rare dry cough. Then
   7-10d ago pt developed a productive cough w/ bloody sputum, not at any
   point bright red blood by itself or clots, or changed over this wk. Pt
   has been having this cough all day and all night, and worsening over
   the course of the wk. Pt has been producing a little over a cup's
   worth/day. The coughing is worse at night when lying flat, and better
   right now after 02 given. Pt does have wheezing, no CP, but does have
   b/l pleuritic pain behind ribs w/ deep breaths. Did not try any
   cough/cold medicatons. No sick contacts. Pt denies any
   fevers/chills/rhinorrhea/congestion/sore throat. Also denies
   epistaxsis, hematemesis, melana, hematochezia. Today his SOB became
   significantly worse, where he could walk about half his baseline
   distance. He called his PCP who told him to come in.
   .
   In the emergency department: P/w 97.5, 115/79, 64, 18,  96%RA. HR was
   into 140s, sinus - got 2L IVF, HR down to 110s-120s. O2 sat mid-90s on
   2L. CTA was ordered intially prelim read showed b/l PEs. Pt was started
   on heparin gtt. This was re-read by attending to no PE, and heparing
   stopped. IP team - no immediate scope. Transferred w/ 96% RA, BPs
   90s-100s. Guaiac neg, no fevers, no pain.
   .
   In the [**Hospital Unit Name 1**], his cough is better.
   Allergies:
   No Known Drug Allergies
   Last dose of Antibiotics:
   Infusions:
   Other ICU medications:
   Other medications:
   - Albuterol Inhaler 2 puffs INH q4-6h PRN
   - ALPHA-1 PROTEINASE INHIB.(HUM) 125 mg/kg +/- 10 % qo week
   - [ADVAIR DISKUS] - 250-50 [**Hospital1 7**]
   - LEVOFLOXACIN 500 mg Tablet 1 Tablet for 1st 5 days of each month
   - MONTELUKAST [SINGULAIR] 10 mg Daily
   - PREDNISONE 20 mg Tablet - 2 Tablets Daily (only when sick)
   - ZOLPIDEM 10 mg Tablet qHS
   Past medical history:
   Family history:
   Social History:
   1. Alpha-1 Anti-Trypsin Deficiency
   2. Emphysema/Asthma
   3. cirrhosis [**2-26**] AAT
   Father died in late 60s from thyroid
   cancer. Mother is a smoker but otherwise healthy.
   Significant for a 20-pack-year history of
   tobacco use.  Quit 15 years. Denies etoh He lives with his mother who
   is also a smoker and has a pet dog.  Worked as a truck-driver
   delivering trucks up anddown the East Coast, now on disability
   Review of systems:  lost 63 lbs s/p gastric bypass banding at [**Hospital1 403**] in
   [**Month (only) **]. Denied nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation or abdominal pain.
   No recent change in bowel or bladder habits. No dysuria. Denied
   arthralgias or myalgias.

   2) Extensive bronchial wall thickening and peribronchial inflammation

Both documents describe the same encounter, yet they contradict each other on a core clinical finding: Document 1 states the patient was admitted with several days of hematuria and underwent cystoscopy, while Document 2 inserts “The patient denies any hematuria.” Temporally the statements refer to the same period, so they are directly incompatible. Semantically they are opposite assertions about the same symptom. Physiologically, a sedated patient cannot reliably deny hematuria, making the denial implausible. Clinically, hematuria logically leads to cystoscopy; the denial disrupts that chain, requiring clarification (e.g., chart vs family report). The conflict is clear, realistic, and highlights a genuine documentation inconsistency.

TITLE: CARDIOLOGY FELLOW CCU ADMISSION NOTE
   Please see housestaff H&P for full details.
   Briefly, this is an 89 year old woman with DM, HTN, and dyslipidemia
   who became acutely short of breath after eating Chinese food.  She
   later developed chest discomfort with associated nausea.   She
   presented to the emergency room where she was tachycardic to 120s,
   hypertensive to the 200s systolic and tachypneic with a respiratory
   rate in the 30s.  She was placed on bipap and a nitroglycerine gtt with
   significant improvement in her breathing.  Cardiac biomarkers were
   positive and EKG showed STE in avR and V1, STD in I, II, avL, V4-V6.
   PE: T97.6          P89                  BP 131/66
   RR20                94% 5L NC
   NAD, speaking in full sentences
   Bilateral crackles to [**12-11**] way up
   JVP 9, RRR, no murmurs
   Abdomen soft, non-tender
   LE warm, no edema
   Neuro
 decreased short term recall
   LABS:
   CK 954 -> 1133                         K 4.6                Co2
   16              BUN     41         Creatinine 1.9
   CKMB 150 -> 154
   Tn 2.56 -> 6.65                          WBC 13.2         HCT
   39.6           Plt 267
   TTE [**2141-2-9**]: The left atrium is normal in size. There is mild symmetric
   left ventricular hypertrophy. The left ventricular cavity size is
   normal. There is mild regional left ventricular systolic dysfunction
   with septal hypokinesis. There is no ventricular septal defect. Right
   ventricular chamber size and free wall motion are normal. The aortic
   root is mildly dilated at the sinus level. The aortic valve leaflets
   are mildly thickened (?#). There is no aortic valve stenosis. Mild (1+)
   aortic regurgitation is seen. The mitral valve leaflets are mildly
   thickened. There is no mitral valve prolapse. Trivial mitral
   regurgitation is seen. Tricuspid regurgitation is present but cannot be
   quantified. There is mild pulmonary artery systolic hypertension. There
   is no pericardial effusion.
   IMPRESSION: Regional LV systolic dysfunction c/w CAD.
   A/P: 89 year old woman with CHF symptoms likely secondary to a primary
   ischemic event.  Given her initial respiratory distress, medical
   optimization was preferred to immediate cardiac catheterization.  After
   a lengthy discussion with Dr. [**Last Name (STitle) 7045**], the patient was initially DNR/DNI;
   she later determined that she wishes to be full code and at this time
   does not wish to pursue cardiac catheterization.
   -          continue heparin gtt, nitroglycerine gtt
   -          diuresis with lasix gtt if no response to IV bolus
   -          continue ASA, betablockade
   -          revisit code status and catheterization with patient
s son
